title: The Hours
events_chronological: In 1923 Richmond, Virginia Woolf begins writing Mrs Dalloway while Leonard and the servants manage her illness.
Virginia's sister Vanessa visits with her children, and a dying bird is buried in the garden.
Virginia tells Leonard at the railway station that she will die if she is kept in Richmond, and he agrees to move back to London.
Virginia decides that her heroine will live and that someone else - a poet - will die instead.
In 1941 Virginia fills her coat pockets with stones and walks into the River Ouse, leaving a letter for Leonard.
In 1951 Los Angeles, the pregnant housewife Laura Brown reads Mrs Dalloway in bed rather than get up for her husband Dan's birthday.
Laura and her small son Richie fail at making a birthday cake and start it again from scratch.
Laura's neighbour Kitty comes to ask her to feed the dog while she goes into hospital, and Laura kisses her.
Laura leaves Richie with a sitter, takes a hotel room and lays out sleeping pills, and then decides to live.
Laura comes home, gets through the birthday dinner, and leaves her family for good once the second baby is born.
In 2001 New York, Clarissa Vaughan buys flowers for a party for her friend Richard, a poet dying of AIDS who calls her Mrs Dalloway.
Clarissa argues with Richard, who will not be consoled and wants neither the party nor the prize.
Richard's former lover Louis Waters visits, and Clarissa breaks down in her kitchen over the summer they were all happy.
Clarissa's daughter Julia and her partner Sally watch her hold the whole day together.
Richard tells Clarissa he stayed alive for her, and lets go of the window ledge.
Laura Brown, now old, arrives from Canada for the wake and tells Clarissa what she did and why.
Clarissa lets Laura stay the night, and Julia takes her upstairs.
Virginia's letter to Leonard is read over all three women: to look life in the face, always, and to put it away.
syuzhet_notes: Three days seventy-eight years apart are cut together as though they were one day, matched on gesture and object - a vase of flowers, a kiss at a kitchen door, an egg cracked in one decade and caught in another. Told-order bullet 1 is a prologue from 1941, eighteen years ahead of the Virginia material that immediately follows it, and the film uses no captions at all, so every jump between 1923, 1951 and 2001 is carried by hair, furniture and light.
fabula_notes: The three strands are not causally simultaneous but are cut as if they were, so a single chronology pulls apart scenes the film deliberately fuses. The link between Laura Brown and Richard - that she is his mother, and that the boy of 1951 is the dying poet of 2001 - is withheld until near the end, and it is what makes this ordering legible at all.
